page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The memory configuration consists of 8.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 1.0 GB per core. Cache specifications include 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core testing placing in the top 25% at 2688.78. Multi-core CPU performance is average, scoring 10787.62 on stress-ng. Memory performance presents a notable tradeoff; while cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 508.47 GB/sec, the Passmark memory score is weak, falling into the bottom 25% at 1424.77. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression also registers as weak at 32.48 GB/sec. Other operations, such as Redis SET at 7.98 million operations per second and static web serving throughput at 7.56 GB/sec, perform within average parameters.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n2d-highcpu-8 offers a high vCPU-to-RAM ratio, making it a cost-effective choice for compute-heavy workloads that do not require large memory footprints. The lack of bundled local storage and GPUs further aligns this server with stateless processing tasks. It is appropriate for workloads such as web serving, software compilation, single-threaded data processing, and lightweight machine learning inference using small models.
